name: Adaptogen Lab — Regulatory Lens Translator
tagline: Same product. Same composition. Rendered compliantly for three markets.
description:
The Regulatory Lens Translator takes a real product composition and renders it as a legitimately compliant label for the EU, US, and Chinese markets — showing not where one regime is stricter, but where regulatory philosophies actually differ. The educational content is the divergence itself: positive-list vs. risk-based vs. two-track categorical. Built on the same grounding architecture that prevents fabricated claims — the same honesty that stops a bad claim also produces a correctly different valid claim depending on where you're standing.

Synthetic-but-structurally-representative rulesets. Verify against primary sources before commercial use. Japan and Korea named as roadmap lenses, not delivered in this build.

schema_json.description: Action grammar for the regulatory_lens_translator agent. Three action types: render a single lens, compare across lenses, flag a specific divergence point.

canonical_document.description: The label claims the user authored — what the product wants to say. This is what gets evaluated. The bill of materials lives beside it in dpp/composition.yaml and is passed to the evaluator as product context, because an ingredient-dependent claim cannot be settled without it. Both are user-editable via PUT /api/workspaces/:id/files/<path>. The legacy single-document path regulatory-lens/sku/{product_id}.yaml is still read as a fallback.

knowledge_asset.description: What the App accumulates. `evaluated/{market}/{claim_id}.yaml` holds one grounding-enforced verdict per claim per market, written by the platform after evaluate_claims runs — not by the agent, so that nothing bypasses the gate. `patterns.yaml` holds cross-claim regulatory patterns and IS the agent's to write. Evaluations carry an `endorsement` field for a qualified reviewer's sign-off, which outranks the agent's own provenance stamp when compare_lenses reads it back.

action_types.description: Render the source composition through a single regulatory lens, producing a valid label for that market with claim renderings, allergen block, divergence notes, and a verification appendix.

target_market.description: Which regulatory lens to render through

claim_ids.description: Specific claim IDs to render. If omitted, renders all source_claims.

include_verification_appendix.description: Include the verification appendix in the output (recommended: always true)

response.action_id: UUID of the action log entry
response.rendered_claims: Array of {claim_id, rendered_text, status, basis, divergence_note}
response.ingredient_status: Array of notable ingredient-status notes for this market

action_types.description: Run the regulatory_lens_translator agent against the live regulatory corpus to evaluate label claims that have not been evaluated yet. This is the only action that produces a verdict for a claim nobody pre-authored — which is every claim a user writes, since claim ids are minted client-side. It calls web_search per market, returns a per-market verdict with citations, and persists the grounding-enforced result to regulatory-lens/ontology/evaluated/{market}/{claim_id}.yaml where compare_lenses will find it. Unlike the other three actions this costs credits and takes seconds per claim; it refuses with 503 if BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY is unset rather than answering from model memory.

claim_ids.description: Claims to evaluate. If omitted, the handler selects the ones with no stored evaluation.

force.description: Re-evaluate claims that already have a stored evaluation. When true, page using the returned `attempted` list — `remaining` will not decrease.

response.evaluated: Array of {claim_id, document, grounding}. `document` carries a verdict block and a separate evidence block per market: <mkt> = {status, basis, rendered_text, needs_expert}, <mkt>_evidence = {queries_run, citations[]}. The two are stamped separately — <mkt>_provenance is model_inference, <mkt>_evidence_provenance is tool_verified or tool_no_match — so a verdict never inherits its citation's strength.
response.skipped: Array of {claim_id, reason, detail} — already evaluated unless force
response.attempted: Claim ids this request took a run at. Page on this, not on `remaining`.
response.remaining: Claims still in scope. At most 3 are evaluated per request.

action_types.description: Read the stored per-market evaluations and produce a side-by-side comparison, optionally focused on a specific claim. This action READS — it is free, instant and involves no agent. A claim reports `not_evaluated` until evaluate_claims has evaluated it.

markets.description: Markets to include in the comparison

claim_id.description: Focus the comparison on a specific claim. If omitted, compares all claims.

include_synthetic_seed.description: Fall back to the shipped ruleset YAMLs for claims with no stored evaluation. Those rulesets are data_status: synthetic_representative — hand-authored sketches of each regime. Off by default so an unevaluated claim reads as unevaluated rather than as answered. Seed rows arrive tagged source: 'synthetic_seed'.

response.comparison_table: Array of {claim_id, candidate_text, markets[], divergence_score, evaluated_markets, markets_in_scope, fully_evaluated}. Each markets[] entry carries source ('agent_evaluation' | 'synthetic_seed' | 'none'), provenance {verdict, evidence}, citations[], queries_run[], needs_expert, endorsed. divergence_score is null unless fully_evaluated — a score across unknowns is not a low score, it is not a score.
response.data_status: What the rows rest on: agent_evaluated_against_live_corpus | synthetic_representative | mixed_agent_evaluated_and_synthetic_seed | unevaluated
response.demo_beat: The scripted demo moment — highest-divergence claim highlighted with one-line regulatory attribution per market

action_types.description: Surface and explain a specific divergence point between two markets on a specific claim or ingredient, attributed to the underlying regulatory philosophy difference.

ingredient_id.description: The ingredient driving the divergence (if ingredient-status divergence)

response.explanation: One-sentence explanation tied to specific regulatory logic — not 'they're stricter'
response.reinstatement: What it would take to make this claim valid in the market where it's currently not allowed

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Lifecycle: changes when regulatory strategy changes, not when recipe changes

# These are candidate claims run through the regulatory lenses (EU, US, CN).
# The compare_lenses action reads this file + composition.yaml and returns
# a grounded comparison showing which claims are allowed in each market.

# Claim status lifecycle:
#   draft → under_review → endorsed → archived
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

data_honesty.caveat: This App now has two sources of truth and every row says which one it came from. (1) AGENT EVALUATION — regulatory_lens_translator searched the live corpus for that specific claim and returned citations. The citations are tool_verified; the verdict over them is model_inference, stamped separately so a status never inherits its citation's strength. Not legal advice, and `needs_expert` marks the ones the agent itself thinks need a human. (2) SYNTHETIC SEED — the shipped ruleset YAMLs, hand-authored to be structurally representative of each regime's logic. These are NOT certified compliance documents and are off by default (`include_synthetic_seed`); a row served from them is tagged `synthetic_seed`. Anything with neither reads `not_evaluated`, which means nobody has looked — never that the claim is permitted. `tool_no_match` likewise means the corpus was searched and had nothing: a gap, not a clearance. Verify against the primary sources below before any commercial use, whichever source a row came from.
data_honesty.what_would_make_a_verdict_stronger: A qualified reviewer signing the `endorsement` field on a stored evaluation, which outranks the agent's own stamp when compare_lenses reads it back. Beyond that, the citations are not yet cross-checked: the platform holds no copy of the EFSA register, 21 CFR or the GB standards, so a cited URL is currently unverified. See CROSS_CHECK_EXEMPTIONS in src/grounding_trust.rs for the two routes out (URL replay, and joining citations to the web_search results of the same episode) and why neither has landed.
